use_cases.pid_tuning: choose or check feedback gains (kp, kd, ki) on a joint
use_cases.bandwidth: closed-loop frequency response: bandwidth, phase lag, margins, resonances
use_cases.delay_id: command and sensing delay (the phase a chirp or multisine reads at high frequency)
use_cases.inertia_id: inertia / armature: the torque that goes with acceleration
use_cases.friction_id: Coulomb, viscous and Stribeck friction, breakaway, cogging
use_cases.gravity_id: gravity torque: masses, centres of mass, mount tilt
use_cases.backlash_id: gear backlash, lost motion and transmission compliance
use_cases.full_dynamics_id: the rigid-body base parameters of a multi-joint chain, all at once
use_cases.tracking_eval: target vs sim vs real tracking error along the motion
use_cases.stop_accuracy: settled error at a stop (Zach's 1 mm tool gate)
use_cases.state_coverage: (q, qd, qdd) cell coverage of a joint: does the data visit where the model must be right
use_cases.workspace_coverage: how much of the reachable workspace (tool positions and orientations) the motion visits
use_cases.repeatability: the same input, run again: the floor every sim-vs-real gate is a multiple of
use_cases.accuracy: absolute pose accuracy against an external truth
use_cases.kinematic_calibration: link lengths, joint zeros and offsets from measured poses
use_cases.homing: finding a joint's zero (hard stops) and getting back to READY from any rest
use_cases.thermal: winding and board temperature: the thermal model and limits
use_cases.endurance: wear, drift and faults over long running (burn-in, life)
use_cases.speed_limits: the speed / acceleration envelope: how fast the joint or tool can go and still track
use_cases.disturbance_rejection: recovery from an external push while holding
use_cases.contact_eval: touching a surface: peak force, bounces, press-force error
use_cases.smoke_test: a quick does-it-work-at-all pass before longer runs
use_cases.collision_check: the motion's swept volume against the robot and the scene
use_cases.cycle_time: how long a task cycle takes (picks per minute)
use_cases.demo: motion that shows the robot off, or shows a person what it can do
use_cases.conveyor_pick_and_place: moving between points that move (a conveyor's): intercept, track at the target's speed, leave

kinds.name: Linear chirp
kinds.one_line: A sine whose frequency rises linearly from f_start to f_end, its amplitude held at a constant speed (angle = v / 2 pi f) or a constant angle (BAM's sin(t^2)), tapered in and out.

prior_art.citation: Pintelon & Schoukens 2012, System Identification: A Frequency Domain Approach, 2nd ed.
MATLAB Simulink Control Design frest.Chirp (linear / logarithmic / quadratic sweep)
ToddlerBot sysID.py: linear chirp 0.1-10 over 10 s, 3 amplitudes x a kp sweep
Rhoban BAM, bam/trajectory.py: lift_and_drop, sin_time_square, up_and_down, sin_sin, half_sine, steps, nothing (read 2026-11-18)

kinds.notes: PID tuna's identification chirp stops at command_rate / 50 (2 Hz at a 100 Hz host): between commands moteus integrates a constant velocity, so a faster chirp breaks J qdd = tau (measured 2026-10-25: 5.7 Hz read a JMC's inertia +50 %, 2 Hz -3 %). BAM's sin(t^2) is this kind from 0 Hz at constant angle (registered as schedule's sin_time_square).

kinds.name: Logarithmic chirp
kinds.one_line: An exponential sweep f0 -> f1 (up or down); at each frequency the amplitude is the smallest of the range, speed and acceleration caps, so it passes through a pendulum's natural mode without leaving the envelope.

prior_art.citation: Farina 2000, AES 108th Convention paper 5093, exponential swept sine
Pintelon & Schoukens 2012, System Identification: A Frequency Domain Approach, 2nd ed.
MATLAB Simulink Control Design frest.Chirp (linear / logarithmic / quadratic sweep)
Beckhoff TE5960 TwinCAT Autotuning, Bode settings: Sine, MultiSine, Chirp, PRBS

kinds.notes: Equal time per octave, so the low band (gravity, friction) and the mode (~3 Hz on CAN 11) both get energy. Above ~1 Hz the acceleration cap sets the amplitude. Stretch lowers the caps, never the band (the band is the point).

kinds.name: Slow sine with a fast ripple
kinds.one_line: A slow large sine with a small fast sine on top: friction that depends on load while moving, and inertia separated from gravity.

prior_art.citation: Rhoban BAM, bam/trajectory.py: lift_and_drop, sin_time_square, up_and_down, sin_sin, half_sine, steps, nothing (read 2026-11-18)
Duclusaud et al. 2024, Extended friction models for the physics simulation of servo actuators (BAM)

kinds.notes: BAM's sin_sin is sin(t) pi/2 + 0.5 sin(5t) sin(2t) over 6 s; ours is the note's F4 rescaled to the joint's range.

kinds.name: Faded sine
kinds.one_line: One sine at a fixed frequency and amplitude (optionally about an offset), faded in and out by raised cosines so it starts and ends at rest where it began.

prior_art.citation: Rhoban BAM, bam/trajectory.py: lift_and_drop, sin_time_square, up_and_down, sin_sin, half_sine, steps, nothing (read 2026-11-18)
Rhoban BAM PR #21, Unitree J288 bam/unitree/all_record.py: torque_chirp 0.25 G, torque_steps 0.5 G, speed_sine, lift_and_damp (read 2026-11-18)
Hwangbo et al. 2019, Science Robotics, actuator-net data from deployment-like sine foot motions (1-25 Hz)

kinds.notes: The 10-24 envelope ladder ran these at rising amplitude and frequency to find the speed and acceleration envelope (the fade exists because a plain sine starts with a velocity step the PD's kd kicks at). BAM's half_sine is one slow cycle; the J288 PR's speed_sine is this kind in velocity mode (kp = 0). trajectory_dataset's 'sweep' class is one faded sine at a random amplitude and frequency.

kinds.name: Stepped sine (sine dwell)
kinds.one_line: A list of frequencies played one after another: ramp in, settle a few cycles, measure amplitude and phase over a few more; the classic point-by-point Bode measurement.

prior_art.citation: MATLAB Simulink Control Design frest.Sinestream (ramp, settle, measure per frequency)
Pintelon & Schoukens 2012, System Identification: A Frequency Domain Approach, 2nd ed.
Beckhoff TE5960 TwinCAT Autotuning, Bode settings: Sine, MultiSine, Chirp, PRBS

kinds.notes: Our code has the single dwell (the runner's faded 'sine' kind with cycles and ramp_cycles); the frequency list is not packaged as one kind yet. Slowest per point of all the frequency-response kinds and the most robust to nonlinearity.

kinds.name: Periodic multisine
kinds.one_line: A periodic sum of sines on a fixed frequency grid (odd lines, every third skipped) with Schroeder phases and equal speed per line, repeated for several periods.

prior_art.citation: Schroeder 1970, IEEE Trans. Inf. Theory 16(1), low-peak-factor multisine phases
Pintelon & Schoukens 2012, System Identification: A Frequency Domain Approach, 2nd ed.
MATLAB System Identification Toolbox idinput: rgs, rbs, prbs, sine
MATLAB Closed-Loop PID Autotuner: sinusoids at 1/10, 1/3, 1, 3, 10 x the target bandwidth
Swevers, Ganseman, Tukel, De Schutter, Van Brussel 1997, IEEE T-RA, Optimal robot excitation and identification

kinds.notes: Periodicity gives a noise floor from the period-to-period spread; the skipped odd lines detect nonlinearity (Pintelon-Schoukens). idinput's 'sine' type is this kind with the lowest-crest of several random phase sets. The MATLAB closed-loop PID autotuner's five sines at 1/10..10 x the target bandwidth is this kind on a sparse grid, added at the plant input while holding.

kinds.name: Orthogonal multisine (every joint at once)
kinds.one_line: Every joint gets its own disjoint set of harmonics of one fundamental, so all joints move together and each joint's response still separates in frequency.

prior_art.citation: Morelli 2003, IFAC, Multiple input design for real-time parameter estimation (orthogonal multisines)
Morelli 2021, NASA NTRS, Practical multiple-input design for aircraft system identification flight tests

kinds.notes: Not in our code. The multi-joint answer to Zach's 11-11 'I don't see a lot of multi-joint motion and coverage' (bam_ur_wrist_coverage multi.py) that keeps per-joint frequency separation.

kinds.name: Pseudo-random binary sequence (PRBS)
kinds.one_line: A maximum-length binary sequence (period 2^n - 1) of two levels, each held one clock period, rate-limited so a position loop can follow it.

prior_art.citation: MATLAB System Identification Toolbox idinput: rgs, rbs, prbs, sine
MATLAB Simulink Control Design frest.PRBS
Beckhoff TE5960 TwinCAT Autotuning, Bode settings: Sine, MultiSine, Chirp, PRBS
PX4 multicopter autotune: a toggling step sequence on the rate setpoint

kinds.notes: Flat spectrum to about 0.44 / clock period. Binary position steps are harsh on a position-controlled joint: drives inject it on the velocity or current loop. PX4's autotune toggles 0 / +A with shrinking holds, a cousin.

kinds.name: Band-limited random noise
kinds.one_line: Gaussian noise filtered to a band and scaled so speed and acceleration stay inside the limits; a new realisation per seed.

prior_art.citation: MATLAB System Identification Toolbox idinput: rgs, rbs, prbs, sine
Pintelon & Schoukens 2012, System Identification: A Frequency Domain Approach, 2nd ed.

kinds.notes: idinput's 'rgs'. Needs windowing or averaging across realisations, where a periodic multisine needs neither.

kinds.name: Optimised Fourier-series excitation
kinds.one_line: Each joint a finite Fourier series of one fundamental, its coefficients optimised under position, speed, acceleration and collision limits to make the dynamics regressor well-conditioned.

prior_art.citation: Swevers, Ganseman, Tukel, De Schutter, Van Brussel 1997, IEEE T-RA, Optimal robot excitation and identification
Gautier & Khalil 1992, IJRR 11(4), Exciting trajectories for the identification of base inertial parameters of robots
Armstrong 1989, IJRR 8(6), On finding exciting trajectories for identification experiments
Calafiore, Indri, Bona 2001, J. Robotic Systems 18(2), optimal excitation trajectories
FloBaRoID: Fourier-series excitation optimised for D-optimality under joint and collision limits
BIRDy (TUM-ICS): generateExcitationTrajectory.m, an optimised Fourier excitation benchmark

kinds.notes: Declared as the sim2real routine arm.dynamics_excitation ('Fourier excitations and the coverage sweep'); no optimiser in our code. FloBaRoID (Python, D-optimality, collision constraints) and BIRDy (MATLAB) are the stock parts. Periodic, so it averages like the multisine.

kinds.name: Biased dither (slide without reversing)
kinds.one_line: A slow constant-speed ramp across the range carrying a small multisine whose speed never exceeds the ramp's, so the joint slides without reversing: inertia and viscous friction with no stick-slip.

prior_art.citation: Wernholt 2004, Linkoping licentiate thesis 1131 (a square-wave offset under the broadband signal)

kinds.name: Open-loop torque chirp
kinds.one_line: With kp = kd = 0, a gravity hold plus a linear torque chirp: the plant with nothing else in the loop.

prior_art.citation: Rhoban BAM PR #21, Unitree J288 bam/unitree/all_record.py: torque_chirp 0.25 G, torque_steps 0.5 G, speed_sine, lift_and_damp (read 2026-11-18)
Pintelon & Schoukens 2012, System Identification: A Frequency Domain Approach, 2nd ed.

kinds.notes: A pendulum only (gravity brings it back); amplitude min(0.25 G, G sin(0.85 x range)) keeps the static deflection in the window. Registered runner=False: needs Zach. Confirmed 2026-11-18 in the J288 PR's all_record.py (0.25 G 'because the chirp sweeps through the pendulum's natural frequency').

kinds.name: Open-loop torque steps
kinds.one_line: Open-loop torque steps (kp = kd = 0) on top of a gravity hold: torque-to-acceleration gain and the friction band with no position loop.

prior_art.citation: Rhoban BAM PR #21, Unitree J288 bam/unitree/all_record.py: torque_chirp 0.25 G, torque_steps 0.5 G, speed_sine, lift_and_damp (read 2026-11-18)

kinds.notes: Not in our code. J288's 0.5 G steps would leave CAN 11's window (Servo Test Schedule note, F9), so size it as torque_chirp is sized.

kinds.name: Free swing (lift and release)
kinds.one_line: Lift the joint under its PD, then release it (torque off, or kd only) and let it coast: inertia, damping and Coulomb friction with no controller in the loop.

prior_art.citation: Rhoban BAM, bam/trajectory.py: lift_and_drop, sin_time_square, up_and_down, sin_sin, half_sine, steps, nothing (read 2026-11-18)
Rhoban BAM PR #21, Unitree J288 bam/unitree/all_record.py: torque_chirp 0.25 G, torque_steps 0.5 G, speed_sine, lift_and_damp (read 2026-11-18)
Duclusaud et al. 2024, Extended friction models for the physics simulation of servo actuators (BAM)

kinds.notes: BAM's lift_and_drop releases after a 2 s cubic lift ('removes back-EMF', the paper); 'nothing' is the torque-off rest; J288's lift_and_damp keeps kd. It ends wherever it comes to rest, so the next segment starts from the measured pose.

kinds.name: Step train
kinds.one_line: Short sharp moves into long holds, alternating sign, with two larger slower steps that cross the friction band: overshoot, ringing and settling are read from it.

prior_art.citation: Astrom & Murray, Feedback Systems, 2nd ed. (step response: rise time, overshoot, settling time)
ArduPilot Copter AutoTune: twitch inputs per axis

kinds.notes: The bandwidth sweep (tune.py) raises the loop's natural frequency one guarded rung at a time on this tape until it rings: a gain ladder is a condition swept over a kind. Sharp because a 50 ms minimum-jerk move has no energy at a 100+ Hz loop's bandwidth.

kinds.name: Staircase (bidirectional levels)
kinds.one_line: Climb to +A in levels, descend to -A, climb back, holding each level, so every inner level is reached once from below and once from above.

prior_art.citation: Rhoban BAM, bam/trajectory.py: lift_and_drop, sin_time_square, up_and_down, sin_sin, half_sine, steps, nothing (read 2026-11-18)
ISO 230-2:2014, positioning accuracy and repeatability of NC axes (bidirectional)
Nordin & Gutman 2002, Automatica 38(10), Controlling mechanical systems with backlash: a survey

kinds.notes: Backlash = the output-camera vs encoder offset between the two approach directions at a settled hold (backlash.py; needs a camera on the output). ISO 230-2's bidirectional positioning (targets from both sides, repeated cycles) is the machine-tool form; BAM's 'steps' is a one-sided staircase.

kinds.name: Doublet and 3-2-1-1 pulses
kinds.one_line: A doublet (+A then -A) or the 3-2-1-1 train (3, 2, 1, 1 time units of alternating sign): a short input with a broad, tunable spectrum.

prior_art.citation: Morelli 1999, J. Aircraft, Flight test of optimal inputs and comparison with conventional inputs (doublet, 3-2-1-1)
Morelli 2021, NASA NTRS, Practical multiple-input design for aircraft system identification flight tests

kinds.notes: Flight-test inputs, used where time on the vehicle is expensive (as arm time is here). Pulse edges need the same rate limit as PRBS.

kinds.name: Relay feedback test
kinds.one_line: Replace the controller by a relay (+d / -d torque on the sign of the error) and read the limit cycle's amplitude and period: the ultimate gain and period a PID rule starts from.

prior_art.citation: Astrom & Hagglund 1984, Automatica 20(5), relay-feedback automatic tuning

kinds.notes: Ku = 4 d / (pi a). Not a precomputed trajectory: the switching follows the measurement. Our tuner starts from an identified model instead (analytic gains, then the step-train sweep).

kinds.name: Rapid replanning
kinds.one_line: A new trajectory every 0.15 s, each starting from the previous one's state at that instant (position and velocity), to seeded targets near home.

prior_art.citation: ROS 2 joint_trajectory_controller, trajectory representation (linear / cubic / quintic spline; replacing a running trajectory)

kinds.notes: Starts and ends at rest; every inner segment joins mid-motion (state handed over), the one join kind no other entry exercises.

kinds.name: Constant-velocity plateaus
kinds.one_line: Constant-speed plateaus out and back at a ladder of speeds, each held long enough to settle: friction against speed (Coulomb, viscous, Stribeck, breakaway).

prior_art.citation: Armstrong-Helouvry, Dupont, Canudas de Wit 1994, Automatica 30(7), friction survey (constant-velocity runs, Stribeck)
Canudas de Wit, Olsson, Astrom, Lischinsky 1995, IEEE TAC 40(3), the LuGre friction model
ODrive anticogging calibration: a slow one-way velocity ramp, then the other way

kinds.notes: PID tuna's ident-sweeps cross the travel at 20-100 % of top speed both ways; sim2real's servo.top_speed_t7 is the top rung (drive ceilings); conveyor.dynamics_profiles fits belt mass and drag from this kind (speed steps and plateaus) on the belt axis. A speed whose plateau would be under 0.8 s is left to the sines. ODrive's anticogging is a slow velocity ramp both ways.

kinds.name: Slow constant-speed triangle (gravity sweep)
kinds.one_line: A slow constant-speed triangle 0 -> +A -> -A -> 0 (or one-sided), corners rounded at a set acceleration: gravity torque, Coulomb friction and the rotor-angle (cogging) map at every angle, both directions.

prior_art.citation: Rhoban BAM, bam/trajectory.py: lift_and_drop, sin_time_square, up_and_down, sin_sin, half_sine, steps, nothing (read 2026-11-18)
Armstrong-Helouvry, Dupont, Canudas de Wit 1994, Automatica 30(7), friction survey (constant-velocity runs, Stribeck)
ODrive anticogging calibration: a slow one-way velocity ramp, then the other way

kinds.notes: Sweeping through the angle where gravity torque changes sign flips the load across the backlash (sim2real arm.backlash_gravity_sweep). integral_study.sweep_q rounds every speed change with a raised cosine of set peak accel. One-sided for a joint that rests on a stop (CAN 13). BAM's up_and_down is the cubic cousin with a static plateau.

kinds.name: Breakaway torque ramp
kinds.one_line: Hold one flank, ramp the torque cap (or feed-forward) until the output leaves, both ways: static friction per direction.

prior_art.citation: Armstrong-Helouvry, Dupont, Canudas de Wit 1994, Automatica 30(7), friction survey (constant-velocity runs, Stribeck)

kinds.name: Small slow reversals at a held pose
kinds.one_line: Small slow back-and-forth moves about a held pose (the load on one flank, then the other): backlash and lost motion, read by an output-side camera or tracker.

prior_art.citation: Nordin & Gutman 2002, Automatica 38(10), Controlling mechanical systems with backlash: a survey

kinds.name: Locked-output torque ramp
kinds.one_line: With the output clamped in a fixture, ramp the motor torque up and down both ways and read the motor angle: backlash and gear stiffness.

prior_art.citation: Nordin & Gutman 2002, Automatica 38(10), Controlling mechanical systems with backlash: a survey

kinds.name: Dithered static pose holds
kinds.one_line: Hold a spread set of poses, dithering slowly in motor space so Coulomb friction cancels, and average the torques: masses, centres of mass and mount tilt by regression.

prior_art.citation: Ma & Hollerbach 1996, ICRA, Identifying mass parameters for gravity compensation

kinds.notes: full_arm.comp_poses draws admitted bent-elbow five-bar poses (fold margin >= 0.1) as the comp's fit and check set; arm.gravity_direction reads the mount tilt from the same holds; servo.known_mass holds a weighed mass for the torque scale. The 11-14 lesson: holds on static friction over-fed the wrist (x1.22); the 15c fit used friction-cancelled MOVING rows.

kinds.name: Minimum-jerk move
kinds.one_line: A rest-to-rest move x = x0 + d (10 s^3 - 15 s^4 + 6 s^5), s = t / T, peaking at 1.875 d / T: the house leg of every waypoints tape.

prior_art.citation: Flash & Hogan 1985, J. Neuroscience 5(7), the minimum-jerk model
Lynch & Park, Modern Robotics, ch. 9: trapezoidal, S-curve, cubic and quintic time scaling

kinds.notes: The runner's waypoints 'q:move_s:dwell_s;...' are minimum-jerk legs that return to the start; its speed check uses the 1.875 peak.

kinds.name: Joint-space waypoints
kinds.one_line: Rest-to-rest moves through a list of absolute joint configurations, each leg timed by one time law, dwelling at each: the classic PTP sequence of a 6-DOF arm, on any joint count.

prior_art.citation: MoveIt 2 Pilz industrial motion planner: PTP (trapezoidal joint profiles, synchronised), LIN and CIRC (trapezoidal in Cartesian space; an arc by centre or interim point)
Robotics Toolbox for Python: jtraj, mtraj, ctraj, mstraj, trapezoidal, quintic
Lynch & Park, Modern Robotics, ch. 9: trapezoidal, S-curve, cubic and quintic time scaling

kinds.notes: Zach 11-18: 'What about like multi waypoint trajectories?' minimum_jerk_move takes fractions of the room around its start; this takes absolute configurations (a pose library, READY, a calibration set).

kinds.name: Trapezoidal velocity move
kinds.one_line: Accelerate at a, cruise at v, decelerate at a (a triangle when the distance is too short to reach v).

prior_art.citation: Lynch & Park, Modern Robotics, ch. 9: trapezoidal, S-curve, cubic and quintic time scaling
Robotics Toolbox for Python: jtraj, mtraj, ctraj, mstraj, trapezoidal, quintic

kinds.name: Jerk-limited S-curve (Ruckig)
kinds.one_line: A time-optimal move to any target state under speed, acceleration and jerk limits (the double-S profile), joints synchronised in time or in phase.

prior_art.citation: Berscheid & Kroger 2021, RSS, Jerk-limited real-time trajectory generation with arbitrary target states (Ruckig)
Ruckig
Biagiotti & Melchiorri 2008, Trajectory Planning for Automatic Machines and Robots (double-S, B-splines)

kinds.notes: Phase synchronisation keeps a multi-joint move straight (memory five-bar-regression, 'Phase, not Time'). bam_trajgen_bench.timelaw is the exact closed form for one joint, held against Ruckig's recorded durations.

kinds.name: Cubic or quintic polynomial move
kinds.one_line: A cubic (position and velocity at both ends) or quintic (plus acceleration) polynomial between two states over a set duration.

prior_art.citation: Lynch & Park, Modern Robotics, ch. 9: trapezoidal, S-curve, cubic and quintic time scaling
Siciliano et al. 2009, Robotics: Modelling, Planning and Control (via-point interpolation)
Robotics Toolbox for Python: jtraj, mtraj, ctraj, mstraj, trapezoidal, quintic
Rhoban BAM, bam/trajectory.py: lift_and_drop, sin_time_square, up_and_down, sin_sin, half_sine, steps, nothing (read 2026-11-18)

kinds.notes: Minimum jerk is the quintic with zero end velocity and acceleration; this kind lets the ends move (joins mid-motion). BAM's up_and_down and lift_and_drop are cubic keyframe splines ([t, x, dx/dt]).

kinds.name: Via-point spline
kinds.one_line: A smooth trajectory through a list of waypoints (spline or blended segments, stopping only where asked), time-parameterised under the limits.

prior_art.citation: ROS 2 joint_trajectory_controller, trajectory representation (linear / cubic / quintic spline; replacing a running trajectory)
Siciliano et al. 2009, Robotics: Modelling, Planning and Control (via-point interpolation)
Robotics Toolbox for Python: jtraj, mtraj, ctraj, mstraj, trapezoidal, quintic
Berscheid & Kroger 2021, RSS, Jerk-limited real-time trajectory generation with arbitrary target states (Ruckig)

kinds.name: Time-optimal path parameterisation
kinds.one_line: Fix the geometric path, then find the fastest timing along it under speed and acceleration (and torque) limits.

prior_art.citation: Pham & Pham 2018, IEEE T-RO 34(3), TOPP-RA
toppra

kinds.notes: The vault's 'Trajectory Controller Archaeology' note records why LERP survived Ruckig on the UR5e cell.

kinds.name: Straight tool line
kinds.one_line: The tool moves on a straight line between two poses with a rest-to-rest time law, mapped to joints by IK at every sample and refused (never clipped) if any sample leaves the envelope.

prior_art.citation: Robotics Toolbox for Python: jtraj, mtraj, ctraj, mstraj, trapezoidal, quintic
ISO 9283:1998, Manipulating industrial robots: performance criteria and related test methods (iso.org page not opened)

kinds.name: Cartesian waypoints
kinds.one_line: The tool visits a list of points or poses and dwells at each; inverse kinematics at the points only, joint-space legs between them (the tool does not move straight between points).

prior_art.citation: MoveIt 2 Move Group interface tutorial: pose goals, joint-space goals and computeCartesianPath (waypoints interpolated at eef_step, IK at every step)
MoveIt 2 Pilz industrial motion planner: PTP (trapezoidal joint profiles, synchronised), LIN and CIRC (trapezoidal in Cartesian space; an arc by centre or interim point)

kinds.notes: The Cartesian twin of joint_waypoints: MoveIt's pose goals in a row. cartesian_straight_line is the straight-line version.

kinds.name: Circular arc of the tool (CIRC)
kinds.one_line: The tool moves on a circular arc from where it is to a goal, the arc set by its centre or by a point it passes through, at rest at both ends, inverse kinematics at every step.

prior_art.citation: MoveIt 2 Pilz industrial motion planner: PTP (trapezoidal joint profiles, synchronised), LIN and CIRC (trapezoidal in Cartesian space; an arc by centre or interim point)
ISO 9283:1998, Manipulating industrial robots: performance criteria and related test methods (iso.org page not opened)

kinds.notes: Pilz's CIRC. circular_test is the full closed circle measured as a ballbar; this is the arc move of the 6-DOF family.

kinds.name: Approach and retreat along the tool axis
kinds.one_line: A straight tool move along its own axis to a pose and back out (or out only): the short linear legs before and after a point, held to the tool's orientation.

prior_art.citation: MoveIt 2 Pilz industrial motion planner: PTP (trapezoidal joint profiles, synchronised), LIN and CIRC (trapezoidal in Cartesian space; an arc by centre or interim point)
MoveIt 2 Move Group interface tutorial: pose goals, joint-space goals and computeCartesianPath (waypoints interpolated at eef_step, IK at every step)

kinds.notes: bam_reach's pick_and_lift recipe is an approach plus a retreat; the axis is the tool's own z unless one is given.

kinds.name: Pose-to-pose move from the reach map
kinds.one_line: Sample a start and a goal pose (optionally a via pose) from the reach map's pose sources, solve IK at the endpoints and time a joint-space move between them.

prior_art.citation: Zacharias, Borst, Hirzinger 2007, IROS, Capturing robot workspace structure (the reachability map)
Berscheid & Kroger 2021, RSS, Jerk-limited real-time trajectory generation with arbitrary target states (Ruckig)

kinds.name: Input-shaped move
kinds.one_line: A move convolved with an impulse sequence (ZV or ZVD) tuned to a lightly damped mode, so it ends with no residual vibration.

prior_art.citation: Singer & Seering 1990, ASME J. Dyn. Sys. Meas. Control 112(1), Preshaping command inputs to reduce system vibration

kinds.name: Joint-space grid snake
kinds.one_line: A boustrophedon tour over a grid of joint levels (the inner joint reverses each row), rest-to-rest moves between waypoints; the held-out tour is an offset grid in shuffled order.

prior_art.citation: Choset 2000, Autonomous Robots 9(3), Coverage of known spaces: the boustrophedon cellular decomposition

kinds.name: Workspace raster sweep
kinds.one_line: The reachable plane cut into square cells, one straight tool row per cell row, boustrophedon, so the tool crosses every reachable cell; timed at a ladder of tool speeds.

prior_art.citation: Choset 2000, Autonomous Robots 9(3), Coverage of known spaces: the boustrophedon cellular decomposition
Zacharias, Borst, Hirzinger 2007, IROS, Capturing robot workspace structure (the reachability map)

kinds.notes: Zach's 'workspace sweep'. The five-bar's real speed ladder runs it vertical and tilted, gravity FF and full FF.

kinds.name: Random reachable targets
kinds.one_line: Seeded uniformly random reachable configurations visited one after another by rest-to-rest moves; another seed is the held-out set.

prior_art.citation: Kavraki, Svestka, Latombe, Overmars 1996, IEEE T-RA 12(4), PRM: uniform random configuration sampling

kinds.notes: Zach, 2026-11-18: 'send it random commands and lets see the performance'. For one joint this is deployment_motion_classes' pickplace; this kind is its multi-joint form.

kinds.name: Space-filling pose set (Sobol, Halton, Latin hypercube)
kinds.one_line: Poses from a low-discrepancy (Sobol, Halton) or stratified (Latin hypercube) sequence over the joint box or the reach map, so N poses cover the space evenly with no clusters.

prior_art.citation: Sobol 1967, USSR Comput. Math. Math. Phys., the Sobol low-discrepancy sequence
Halton 1960, Numerische Mathematik, the Halton sequence
McKay, Beckman, Conover 1979, Technometrics, Latin hypercube sampling
scipy.stats.qmc.Sobol

kinds.notes: sim2real's homing bench draws its start states from a Sobol sequence. Sobol wants N = 2^m points.

kinds.name: Lissajous (incommensurate sines per joint)
kinds.one_line: Each joint a sine at its own frequency, the frequencies near-incommensurate, so the joint-space curve fills the box densely with smooth periodic motion.

prior_art.citation: Bazaei, Yong, Moheimani 2012, Rev. Sci. Instrum. 83, Lissajous-scan pattern planning (AFM)

kinds.notes: Only scan-pattern prior art found (AFM), no robot-identification paper. A Lissajous curve is a one-line-per-joint multisine, so it inherits that analysis; it is also the prettiest landing-page demo of coverage.

kinds.name: Coverage-picked tapered swings
kinds.one_line: Tapered sine swings, one per (centre, amplitude, frequency), picked greedily by how many empty (q, qd, qdd) cells each adds until the predicted coverage clears a target.

prior_art.citation: Isaac Sim system identification: sine sweeps, multisines, splines, and a separate validation trajectory

kinds.notes: The only kind chosen BY the coverage metric (sim2real.schedule.joint.occupancy): Zach's 11-04 gate, 'bin the space and check that X % of cells are covered'. On the five-bar crank it lifted C1 from 34.1 % toward the proposed 40 %.

kinds.name: Repeat-floor tape
kinds.one_line: One frozen tape played N times with the same input: the run-to-run floor every sim-vs-real gate is a multiple of.

prior_art.citation: ISO 9283:1998, Manipulating industrial robots: performance criteria and related test methods (iso.org page not opened)
Bristow, Tharayil, Alleyne 2006, IEEE Control Systems Magazine 26(3), A survey of iterative learning control

kinds.notes: Pendulum contract: REPEATS = 5 per rung; sim vs real must be <= 1.5x the same-input repeat floor (pendulum_goal.py on lane claude/1dof-rack-sim-to-real-435fc0-v4, not on main). Repeating one trajectory is also what iterative learning control feeds on.

kinds.name: A-to-B speed ladder
kinds.one_line: Minimum-jerk A -> B -> A moves whose peak speed is a rising fraction of the joint's top speed, each rung repeated, plus held-out A/B pairs: tracking and stop accuracy as speed rises to the motor's limit.

prior_art.citation: ISO 9283:1998, Manipulating industrial robots: performance criteria and related test methods (iso.org page not opened)
ANSI/RIA R15.05-1, point-to-point and static performance characteristics of industrial robots

kinds.notes: The pendulum campaign's frozen contract (pendulum_goal.py RUNG_FRACTIONS / REPEATS / HELD_OUT, lane claude/1dof-rack-sim-to-real-435fc0-v4). The rack's 'tape' kind is a raised-cosine out-and-back per speed. ISO 9283 also runs its pose tests at several rated speeds.

kinds.name: ISO 9283 pose test (cube, P1-P5)
kinds.one_line: Five poses on a diagonal plane of a cube in the workspace, visited in order for many cycles, each approached from the same direction: pose accuracy, repeatability, stabilisation time and overshoot.

prior_art.citation: ISO 9283:1998, Manipulating industrial robots: performance criteria and related test methods (iso.org page not opened)
ISO 9283:1998 scope listing (pose accuracy and repeatability, stabilisation time, overshoot, path accuracy, cornering)
ANSI/RIA R15.05-1, point-to-point and static performance characteristics of industrial robots

kinds.notes: P1-P5 and 30 cycles are from memory of the standard, not re-read (paywalled). Our encoder-scored workspace sweeps (r1a-r1d, 11-17) are the house version, scored by sim2real.metrics.actuator.stops; Zach's gate is 1 mm PER STOP, stricter than ISO's mean.

kinds.name: ISO 9283 path test (line, circle, corners)
kinds.one_line: A straight line, a circle and a rectangle's corners traced at set tool speeds: path accuracy, path repeatability, cornering deviation and speed fidelity.

prior_art.citation: ISO 9283:1998, Manipulating industrial robots: performance criteria and related test methods (iso.org page not opened)
ISO 9283:1998 scope listing (pose accuracy and repeatability, stabilisation time, overshoot, path accuracy, cornering)

kinds.name: Circular test (ballbar)
kinds.one_line: A circle traced by two axes together (two joints, or the tool in a plane), in both directions: circular error and the spikes at each axis reversal.

prior_art.citation: ISO 230-4:2022, circular tests for NC machine tools

kinds.notes: The quadrant reversals show backlash and friction as spikes, which makes it a cheap two-joint backlash screen.

kinds.name: Kinematic calibration pose set
kinds.one_line: Static poses chosen to make the calibration's identification Jacobian well-conditioned (an observability index), each measured by an external tracker or camera.

prior_art.citation: Borm & Menq 1991, IJRR 10(1), optimal measurement configurations by an observability measure
Sun & Hollerbach 2008, ICRA, Observability index selection for robot calibration
Hollerbach & Wampler 1996, IJRR 15(6), The calibration index and taxonomy for robot kinematic calibration

kinds.notes: bam_calibration samples leader configurations on the assembled five-bar branch and rejects branch-ambiguous ones (real data never rides the fold). Zach's 2024-03 notebook: system ID on ~20 parameters (lengths plus backlash), not thousands.

kinds.name: Hand-eye station set
kinds.one_line: Stations spread over the whole workspace (left and right) with large rotations between them, a marker or board seen at each: AX = XB hand-eye, then a held-out check-set to refit and validate.

prior_art.citation: Tsai & Lenz 1989, IEEE T-RA 5(3), fully autonomous and efficient 3D robotics hand/eye calibration
Park & Martin 1994, IEEE T-RA, Robot sensor calibration: solving AX = XB on the Euclidean group

kinds.notes: Zach (DP - Hand Eye Calibration, 11-13): cover the whole workspace; accuracy plateaus after X poses. The 11-15 overhead D435 fit on 4 runs at one J1 angle overfit (0.88 px own, 4-9 px held out); the refit over J1 -5..-30 deg halved held-out error.

kinds.name: Calibration board views
kinds.one_line: A ChArUco board (carried by the arm, or fixed and seen from a camera the arm carries) at many tilts and positions across the image: intrinsics and distortion.

prior_art.citation: Zhang 2000, IEEE TPAMI 22(11), A flexible new technique for camera calibration

kinds.name: Hard-stop seek (homing)
kinds.one_line: One joint pushes toward its hard stop at a slow slewed setpoint under a low torque cap that steps up, the others held, until it stalls at the top cap; that angle defines the zero (one touch, N touches averaged, or press-probe-re-press).
kinds.notes: Zach's procedure (11-10): J2 to its stop, then C1, then J1. A stall at a low cap may be gravity or friction, so the cap steps up; a stall at the top cap is the stop wherever it is, never an assumed angle. Needs no limits: it is what finds them.

kinds.name: Return to READY
kinds.one_line: A JointCommandSequence that walks the arm from wherever it rests to READY along waypoints that keep fold margins, then settles: the rig's recover-yourself move.
kinds.notes: Zach 11-11: recover a stuck arm yourself with the return-to-home JointCommandSequence. The past-straight fold escape (11-15) is a variant whose first step picks the escape direction.

kinds.name: Burn-in wiggle
kinds.one_line: Each joint walked to its homed zero, then swept about it one at a time at rising speeds with the others held, then gripper open/close cycles, every tick logged (current, bus voltage, board temperature, faults).
kinds.notes: Zach's step 3 (11-13): 'burn-in wiggle ... with no faults'. A PASS needs the joint to have tracked its sweep, every pose checked against the self-collision guard first. Defaults are 25 deg at 20 / 40 / 60 deg/s.

kinds.name: Winding heating run
kinds.one_line: Hold the rotor at standstill with a constant d-axis current, read the winding temperature from its resistance between heats, then log the cool-down: the motor's thermal model.

prior_art.citation: IEC 60034-1 rotating electrical machines, duty types S1-S10 (preview)

kinds.notes: A current, not a motion (the rotor holds stepper-fashion); its temperatures are provisional until checked against a thermometer.

kinds.name: Endurance duty cycle
kinds.one_line: A deployment cycle (or a duty-type profile) repeated for hours with logging and periodic gap checks: wear, drift and thermal steady state.

prior_art.citation: IEC 60034-1 rotating electrical machines, duty types S1-S10 (preview)

kinds.notes: sim2real servo.gap_check_forecast: the deployed backlash check every 12 h on the daily motions. MOC - Testing Robotic Systems lists 'gripper cycle-forever'.

kinds.name: Power-up from random rests
kinds.one_line: Start states drawn where a hand or a fall can leave the arm (singular and flipped rests oversampled), then home or recover from each: robustness of the power-up path.

prior_art.citation: Kavraki, Svestka, Latombe, Overmars 1996, IEEE T-RA 12(4), PRM: uniform random configuration sampling

kinds.notes: Sim only by design (the arm falls unpowered into its rest); the start states, not a trajectory, are the generated part.

kinds.name: Deployment motion classes (pickplace, cycle, jog, sweep)
kinds.one_line: Seeded random tapes in four deployment classes: pickplace (large moves, long holds), cycle (one pair out and back x3), jog (small corrections) and sweep (one slow pass); other seeds are the sealed held-out set.

prior_art.citation: Hwangbo et al. 2019, Science Robotics, actuator-net data from deployment-like sine foot motions (1-25 Hz)
Isaac Sim system identification: sine sweeps, multisines, splines, and a separate validation trajectory

kinds.notes: PID tuna scores every candidate gain set on these (a different seed is the held-out set, so a pick is never proven on the tape it was chosen on); the rack schedule's OPERATE set and H2 acceptance set are the same classes.

kinds.name: Pick-and-place cycle
kinds.one_line: Approach above, pre-grasp, a two-stage descent (hover, settle, slow final line), close, lift, carry, place, release, return: the cycle the facility runs, scored in picks per minute.

prior_art.citation: Calli et al. 2015, IEEE RAM, The YCB object and model set: benchmarking in manipulation research
Kimble et al. 2020, IEEE RA-L 5(2), Benchmarking protocols for evaluating small parts robotic assembly systems

kinds.notes: Zach 11-12: don't score traj gen on facility KPIs; keep its own (SPPM in bam_trajgen_bench). The two-stage descent is pick_stops' fix for cogging error on a long descent.

kinds.name: Approach and track a moving point
kinds.one_line: From rest, meet a point that moves (a pose as a function of time) at the sync time with its velocity matched, then follow it within tolerance to the end of the sync window, then come to rest.
kinds.notes: Zach 11-18: 'You can account for like trajectory points that are moving'. Contract and ruler: robot_trajectories.moving (synchronised). bam_grasp's conveyor leads the target by 0.25 s to cancel servo lag.

kinds.name: Track, then leave a moving point
kinds.one_line: Already moving with a point, keep with it for a dwell in its frame, then leave it along a direction to rest: the second half of a moving-target cycle.

kinds.name: U between points that move
kinds.one_line: The U of pick_and_place_cycle (approach, down, dwell, up, over, down, dwell, up) where the first point moves: down and up are tracked in the point's frame, synchronised at the bottom.
kinds.notes: bam_grasp's conveyor line delivered 19/40 on a moving belt against 30/40 static: the loss is tracking error along the belt, which this kind's sync window makes a measured, gated number.

kinds.name: Adept cycle
kinds.one_line: The industry cycle-time benchmark: 25 mm up, 305 mm across, 25 mm down and back (extended: 25 / 700 / 25 mm).

prior_art.citation: Omron/Adept iX4 manual: the Adept cycle, 25 mm up, 305 mm across, 25 mm down
Schneider Lexium Cobot typical cycle time (Adept cycle, arrival within 0.25 mm)

kinds.notes: The vendor-neutral number benchmark robots publish; bam_trajgen_bench's profiles (Glacier, AMP, Recycleye) are scored on SPPM.

kinds.name: Touch-down on a surface
kinds.one_line: Descend from above a surface, the last stretch at a constant touch speed aiming slightly below it, dwell in contact, lift: peak force, bounces and press-force error.
kinds.notes: robot_controllers' R3 belt-impact rungs at 0.05 / 0.10 / 0.20 m/s on a belt moving 0.25 m/s.

kinds.name: Hold and read the settled stop
kinds.one_line: Hold the last target for a set time and read the settled stop from the hold's final window: the segment that joins two moves, and the stop-accuracy reading itself.

prior_art.citation: ISO 9283:1998, Manipulating industrial robots: performance criteria and related test methods (iso.org page not opened)
ISO 230-2:2014, positioning accuracy and repeatability of NC axes (bidirectional)

kinds.notes: Zach's 1 mm tool gate at a settled stop (sim2real.result.TOOL_GATE_MM). Approaching every stop from one fixed side (the 11-15 READY aim: 1.48 -> 0.38 mm) is a parameter of the hold, as ISO 230-2's unidirectional approach is.

kinds.name: Hold under a push
kinds.one_line: Hold a pose and push it (a set force for a set time in sim, by hand on the rig): recovery time and overshoot.

prior_art.citation: moteus PID tuning guide: hold a position and disturb it by hand

kinds.notes: The trajectory is a plain hold; the generated part is the disturbance schedule beside it (a sim force, or a cue to push).

kinds.name: Weightless float
kinds.one_line: Hold a pose under PD with gravity feed-forward, then drop kp and kd to zero and keep sending the gravity torque: the drift over the float window is how well gravity is modelled.

prior_art.citation: Ma & Hollerbach 1996, ICRA, Identifying mass parameters for gravity compensation

kinds.notes: 'It feels weightless' made measurable (deg/s of drift); hardware-proven on the gravity-comp package (-0.06 deg drift).
